name: Racecadotril
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Racecadotril is an enkephalinase inhibitor for acute diarrhea, converted to the active metabolite thiorphan; racecadotril is eliminated mainly in urine as metabolites (81.4% of the dose; SmPC 5.2). The Irish label has limited data in kidney impairment and advises caution without a dose change; courses are limited to 7 days. Combining it with ACE inhibitors raises the risk of angioedema. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: The SmPC does not grade kidney impairment; bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Adults: 100 mg initially, then 100 mg three times daily before main meals until two normal stools; no more than 7 days (SmPC).
Limited data in kidney impairment; use with caution (SmPC). No dose change is specified. Racecadotril is eliminated mainly in urine as metabolites (81.4% of the dose; SmPC 5.2).

hd.text: No dialysis data. Short course only if needed; specialist judgment.

monitoring: Hydration (racecadotril is an adjunct to rehydration). Stop at once for severe skin reactions (DRESS). Avoid with ACE inhibitors and other angioedema-promoting drugs. Bloody stools or fever need investigation (SmPC 4.4).

pediatric.approved_ages: Capsules: adults only. Pediatric granules exist; their SmPC was not retrieved.
pediatric.usual_dose: Not covered by the capsule SmPC.
